You will sit at the intersection of Product, Finance, Data, Growth, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Operations. You will combine customer research, behavioral data, market intelligence, financial analysis, and experimentation to shape HighLevel’s commercial strategy.

This is not an advisory-only role. You will be expected to develop recommendations, build alignment, support implementation, measure results, and improve decisions based on what we learn.

The role reports to the Chief of Staff and will have significant exposure to HighLevel’s executive leadership team.
What you will own
Pricing and packaging strategy

Develop a clear, company-wide pricing and packaging strategy across subscription plans, product bundles, add-ons, usage-based capabilities, services, and new product launches.

Evaluate how HighLevel’s pricing architecture should evolve as the platform expands into new products, customer segments, and monetization models.

Identify the most appropriate value metrics for different parts of the platform, including where subscription, usage-based, account-based, feature-based, or hybrid pricing models may be appropriate.

Assess opportunities to improve plan differentiation, feature entitlements, upgrade paths, product bundling, and add-on attachment.

Build business cases for pricing and packaging changes, including expected impact on acquisition, trial-to-paid conversion, average revenue per customer, expansion, retention, gross margin, and lifetime value.

Develop principles and guardrails for discounts, promotions, trials, grandfathering, migrations, and price increases.

Partner with Finance and Data teams to model revenue impact, customer impact, adoption scenarios, and potential risks.

Create a prioritized monetization roadmap rather than treating pricing as a series of isolated decisions.

Customer research and insights

Build a continuous customer research program covering prospects, trial users, paying customers, expanded customers, churned customers, agency owners, affiliates, and the businesses operating within agency sub-accounts.

Establish a clear segmentation framework based on customer needs, behaviors, maturity, business models, use cases, value realization, and willingness to pay.

Lead qualitative and quantitative research, including customer interviews, surveys, concept testing, win/loss analysis, churn research, behavioral analysis, and willingness-to-pay studies.

Understand the jobs customers hire HighLevel to perform, the outcomes they value, the alternatives they consider, and the barriers that prevent them from adopting or expanding.

Create a centralized customer-insights repository so that research is accessible, reusable, and connected to company decisions.

Develop a regular cadence for sharing insights with Product, Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, and executive leadership.

Translate research into clear implications for product strategy, roadmap prioritization, positioning, onboarding, customer education, and go-to-market execution.

Experimentation and implementation

Design pricing, packaging, positioning, and offer experiments with clearly defined hypotheses, target segments, success metrics, and decision criteria.

Partner with Product, Growth, Engineering, Billing, Legal, Finance, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success to operationalize approved changes.

Develop rollout strategies that account for existing customers, new customers, channel partners, affiliates, billing complexity, communications, and customer support.

Establish guardrails to ensure that monetization initiatives improve business performance without creating unacceptable deterioration in customer trust, conversion, adoption, or retention.

Build post-launch measurement plans and ensure that each major pricing or packaging decision generates reusable learning.

Monitor performance across metrics such as trial-to-paid conversion, plan mix, average revenue per customer, add-on attachment, expansion, downgrade rates, churn, net revenue retention, gross margin, and customer lifetime value.

Market and competitive intelligence

Maintain a structured view of pricing, packaging, positioning, and monetization trends across relevant SaaS, agency technology, CRM, marketing automation, communications, AI, and adjacent software categories.

Identify changes in customer expectations, competitive offers, business models, and emerging value metrics.

Distinguish between competitive signals that require action and those that should not influence HighLevel’s strategy.

Use market intelligence as one input alongside customer value, product strategy, economics, and HighLevel’s long-term differentiation.

Decision-making and organizational leadership

Establish a cross-functional pricing and monetization operating cadence, including clear decision rights, approval processes, and measurement standards.

Bring structure to complex decisions where customer needs, product strategy, technical constraints, and financial outcomes may conflict.

Present recommendations to senior leaders in a clear, commercially grounded, and decision-oriented manner.

Build alignment across functions while remaining willing to challenge assumptions and surface difficult trade-offs.

Initially operate as a hands-on leader and, as the function develops, help define and build the right team across pricing, monetization analytics, and customer insights.

Raise the organization’s overall capability in customer research, pricing strategy, experimentation, and value-based decision-making.
What we are looking for
14+ years of experience across SaaS pricing, monetization, product strategy, customer insights, growth strategy, management consulting, corporate strategy, or related roles.

Significant direct experience leading pricing and packaging decisions for a B2B SaaS, platform, or technology company.

Demonstrated experience translating customer research and data into changes in product, pricing, packaging, or go-to-market strategy.

Strong understanding of SaaS business models, including subscription economics, usage-based pricing, expansion revenue, retention, gross margin, and customer lifetime value.

Experience working with multi-product or multi-tier offerings and navigating the impact of pricing changes on existing and new customers.

Strong quantitative and financial modeling skills, with the ability to develop scenarios, challenge assumptions, and make recommendations with imperfect information.

Experience with both qualitative and quantitative research methods, such as customer interviews, segmentation, surveys, willingness-to-pay analysis, concept testing, conjoint analysis, and behavioral data analysis.

Strong commercial judgment and the ability to balance customer value, growth, simplicity, operational feasibility, and long-term strategy.

Excellent executive communication skills, including the ability to turn complex analysis into a clear recommendation and decision.

A highly collaborative working style and a record of influencing Product, Finance, Data, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success leaders.

Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where the operating model and analytical foundation may still need to be built.

A player-coach mentality: equally comfortable defining strategy, conducting customer interviews, reviewing analyses, building a business case, and supporting execution.
Preferred experience
Experience with product-led growth, free trials, self-serve acquisition, or hybrid product-led and sales-assisted models.

Experience with agency software, SMB software, CRM, marketing automation, communications, payments, AI products, or vertical SaaS.

Experience with ecosystems in which the direct customer serves or resells products to another end customer.

Experience with white-label products, reseller models, marketplaces, channel partners, or multi-sided platforms.

Experience launching usage-based products or monetizing high-variable-cost capabilities such as communications, payments, infrastructure, or AI.

Familiarity with SQL, experimentation platforms, business intelligence tools, or product analytics systems.

Experience building a pricing, customer insights, or monetization function from an early stage
What success looks like
In the first 90 days

Develop a clear understanding of HighLevel’s customer segments, current plans, product entitlements, monetization model, customer economics, and decision-making processes.

Complete an initial assessment of pricing and packaging opportunities, risks, customer pain points, and analytical gaps.

Establish a customer research agenda across trial users, paying customers, expanded customers, churned customers, agencies, affiliates, and sub-accounts.

Create an initial pricing and packaging opportunity backlog, distinguishing near-term improvements from longer-term strategic questions.

Establish a cross-functional pricing and monetization governance process.

Within six months

Deliver a practical customer segmentation and needs framework that is actively used by Product and go-to-market teams.

Establish a repeatable customer research and insight-sharing cadence.

Present a prioritized pricing and packaging roadmap supported by customer evidence, behavioral data, competitive context, and financial modeling.

Launch or support the launch of the first major pricing, packaging, or monetization initiative.

Implement reporting that connects pricing decisions to customer and business outcomes.

Within the first year

Establish a clear and scalable pricing architecture across HighLevel’s core platform, add-ons, and emerging products.

Build a trusted customer-insights capability that consistently informs product, go-to-market, and strategic decisions.

Create a repeatable process for researching, testing, launching, and evaluating monetization changes.

Deliver measurable improvement across one or more key outcomes, such as trial-to-paid conversion, plan mix, average revenue per customer, product attachment, expansion, retention, net revenue retention, or gross margin.

Build strong organizational confidence that major pricing and product decisions are grounded in customer value, sound economics, and rigorous learning.
Why this role matters
HighLevel’s pricing and packaging decisions influence far more than revenue. They shape which customers we attract, how quickly customers understand the platform, which products they adopt, how agencies build businesses on top of HighLevel, and how effectively we can continue investing in customer value.

This role will help create the customer understanding and commercial discipline required for HighLevel’s next stage of growth.

jobs.description:
About us
HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes.
To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently.
Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.

Our people
With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our impact
Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.
Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts

Who You AreYou are a hands-on enablement builder. You are energised by walking into a function that is scaling fast, mapping how work actually gets done today, and turning it into documented process, a structured curriculum, and a certification standard that holds up when the team doubles.
You have personally built training programs from a blank page — not bought them, not briefed an agency on them. You have written the SOP, built the learning path, run the facilitation, scored the calls, and sat with a struggling advisor to close the gap. You think in frameworks and operating rhythms, and you can equally sit in a live onboarding call and tell exactly where the advisor lost the customer.
In this role you own capability for HighLevel's Customer Success department — both the Implementation team that runs a customer's first weeks on the platform and the CSM team that owns the relationship for life. You will lead a small enablement team (trainers and QA analysts) and partner closely with frontline managers, who remain accountable for performance while you are accountable for the systems that make good performance repeatable.
This is a craft and capability role, not a commercial one. Success here is measured in ramp time, process adherence, call quality, and product depth — not in numbers carried.
What You'll Be Doing
HighLevel's Customer Retention and Account Management teams play a critical role in helping customers realize value, maintain their subscriptions, and grow their businesses through the platform.

As a Senior Enablement Partner, you will develop and deliver training, coaching, and learning resources that strengthen customer engagement, retention, winback, and account expansion. You'll work closely with frontline leadership to identify performance gaps, build practical solutions, and reinforce the skills and behaviors that contribute to improved business outcomes.

You will:

Independently manage assigned enablement initiatives, from identifying business and performance needs through program design, implementation, and evaluation, in alignment with the revenue enablement strategy and organizational priorities.

Leverage AI-powered tools to develop training content, create realistic practice scenarios, support coaching, and improve the efficiency and effectiveness of enablement programs.

Design, deliver, and continuously improve onboarding programs, learning paths, and certifications for Customer Retention and Account Management teams.

Build and facilitate ongoing training programs focused on discovery, consultative selling, objection handling, negotiation, customer retention, winback, and account expansion.

Create and maintain playbooks, talk tracks, SOPs, and coaching resources that support consistent customer-facing execution.

Analyze call recordings, CRM data, and performance trends to diagnose execution gaps, distinguish training needs from operational challenges, and develop targeted enablement solutions.

Partner with frontline managers to reinforce effective coaching practices and strengthen the application of trained behaviors.

Develop practical assessments, role-playing exercises, and coaching activities that improve seller confidence and skill proficiency.

Collaborate with Product, Product Marketing, and Revenue Operations to support product launches, process changes, and adoption of sales tools.

Evaluate enablement effectiveness using established learning, behavioral, and business performance measures, including retention, winback, and account expansion outcomes.

Advise Customer Retention and Account Management leaders on performance trends, capability gaps, and recommended improvements within assigned areas of enablement expertise.

Explore and apply new learning methods and technologies, including AI-assisted coaching and interactive learning experiences, to improve training effectiveness.
What You'll Bring
Experience designing and delivering sales enablement, customer success, or professional training programs, preferably in SaaS or high-growth environments.

Experience using AI-powered tools to support content development, learning design, coaching, or other enablement activities, with the ability to evaluate and refine AI-generated outputs.

Strong understanding of customer retention, account management, consultative selling, and revenue expansion practices.

Experience creating onboarding programs, learning paths, playbooks, and coaching resources.

Strong facilitation, coaching, presentation, and written communication skills.

Ability to analyze performance data, identify skill gaps, and translate findings into practical training solutions.

Experience partnering with frontline managers and cross-functional stakeholders to improve team performance.

Proficiency with CRM platforms, learning management systems, and sales enablement tools.

Ability to independently manage assigned projects, adapt to changing priorities, and deliver high-quality learning experiences.

Bachelor's degree in Business, Education, Communications, or a related field with typically 5+ years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and practical experience.

Demonstrated experience developing and delivering training, coaching, or enablement programs.

Certifications in instructional design, adult learning, or sales methodologies preferred.

This is a build role. You will be creating the foundation of knowledge and growth for the entire affiliate organization from the ground-up while collaborating with senior affiliate leadership. Own onboarding for every new affiliate manager joining the affiliate team, resulting in time-to-first-activation results amongst growing affiliate managers and “exams” to ensure proficiency is maintained across the entire organization

Create and maintain a centralized internal resource hub — an always-current repository of playbooks, SOPs, and tools that every AFM can access in seconds.
Design and own the structured onboarding experience for all new affiliates outside the endorsed tier
Build and maintain the product knowledge baseline, establishing what a “qualified affiliate manager” knows about the product, the program, and strategies about our top affiliates
Collaborate with Affiliate Partner individuals to build lifecycle communication sequences (email, SMS, in-app) that guide new affiliates from sign-up through first trial
Work cross-functionally to ensure that the process for new affiliates is constantly being optimized for broader team goals
Provide reports for senior leadership, finance, revenue operations, and other stakeholders as needed
Attend affiliate industry events, conferences, and meetups — representing GHL and building direct relationships with existing and prospective affiliate partners.

Willingness and ability to travel for events, affiliate meetups, and in-person team sessions.
Proficiency with CRM (HighLevel or similar), call intelligence tools (Olive AI, Gong, Chorus, or equivalent), and communication/outreach platforms highly preferred.
Direct experience working inside a SaaS affiliate or partner program is highly preferred.
Strong English written and verbal communication.
Dallas-based or willing to travel to Dallas frequently. Frequent in-office presence expected.

4–6 years of experience in affiliate program management, channel partner enablement, sales enablement, or a directly adjacent role.
Thorough experience building onboarding programs, call frameworks, or coaching toolkits from scratch.
Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, or equivalent practical experience.

Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts
Role overview
We are seeking a Senior Manager, Product Design to lead design for HighLevel's core platform experiences, mobile experiences for native platforms and design system team. This role will report to the Senior Director, Product Design and manage approximately 8 product designers across the United States and India.
This is a craft-driven senior design manager role for someone who can help create a step change in HighLevel's design practice. The ideal candidate brings exceptional aesthetic judgment, visual craft and interaction-design taste, plus the leadership ability to turn those standards into better work from the team.
A major part of this role will be line managing the design system team and helping level up design system strategy and execution, in partnership with the Senior Director, Product Design, who owns the design system as part of their broader portfolio. The goal is not only better internal tooling, but major improvements to the UX/UI our customers experience every day.
HighLevel values velocity, ownership and practical innovation. We are actively adopting AI-assisted production workflows, including tools such as Cursor and Claude Code, and we are looking for design leaders who are curious about new ways of working and eager to help teams get to better results more quickly.
Product and design scope
You will lead design execution and quality across three connected areas:
Core platform experiences that help agencies and SMBs manage customers, work across accounts, navigate the product, configure settings and complete essential business workflows
Mobile experiences for native platforms that make HighLevel's most important workflows accessible, focused and effective for customers on the go
Design system strategy, execution and team practices, including AI-assisted production workflows, that help designers and engineers deliver a vastly better, more consistent customer experience
What you will lead
A team of approximately 8 product designers across US and India teams, including coaching, career development, performance management, prioritization and staffing
Design quality and execution across core platform experiences, native mobile surfaces and design system work
Line management for the design system team, in partnership with the Senior Director on design system strategy, priorities and adoption
A high-velocity operating rhythm for critiques, reviews, planning, feedback loops and cross-functional alignment
A meaningfully higher bar for aesthetic quality, visual design, interaction design, information architecture, product thinking and end-to-end usability
Talent development, including elevating strong performers and supporting designers who need clearer expectations or additional coaching
Key responsibilities
1. Team leadership and management
Manage, coach and develop approximately 8 product designers across US and India teams
Set clear expectations for quality, ownership, collaboration and delivery
Hire excellent talent, onboard new designers and help the team grow with intention
Elevate designers through coaching, stretch opportunities and clear development plans
Performance manage thoughtfully and directly when designers need additional support, sharper expectations or role calibration
Build a team culture that values speed, ownership, craft and customer impact
2. Craft, aesthetic quality and product excellence
Raise the bar for design output across aesthetic quality, visual craft, interaction quality, product design thinking and customer-centered execution
Help create a step change in HighLevel's design practice by making quality standards sharper, more visible and more consistently applied
Lead critiques and quality reviews that improve the work before it reaches customers
Ensure major releases are grounded in clear user needs, thoughtful flows, durable interaction patterns and refined visual execution
Encourage responsible use of AI-assisted tools and workflows to accelerate exploration, prototyping, documentation and production collaboration
3. Core platform and mobile design leadership
Lead design execution across core platform experiences that support navigation, account management, configuration, workflow execution and customer operations
Guide mobile design for native platforms, ensuring the experience is focused, useful and appropriately adapted to mobile customer needs
Partner with Product and Engineering to clarify priorities, shape roadmaps, identify tradeoffs and maintain a high-quality customer experience
Connect work across desktop, mobile and shared platform surfaces so customers experience HighLevel as one coherent product
4. Design system leadership
Line manage the design system team and help evolve HighLevel's bespoke design system into a strategic accelerator for product quality, execution speed and customer experience
Partner with the Senior Director on design system strategy, priorities, governance and adoption across the broader product portfolio
Work horizontally across product, design and engineering teams to drive adoption of shared components, patterns and interaction standards
Reduce pattern drift across core platform and mobile experiences through clear guidance, reusable patterns and strong examples of the desired UX/UI quality
5. Cross-functional collaboration and business impact
Build strong operating partnerships with Product, Engineering, Data, Support and Customer Success
Represent design in planning, roadmap and delivery conversations with clarity and sound product judgment
Work effectively across time zones and cultures, especially between US and India teams
Model the pace, ownership and adaptability expected in a high-velocity product environment
Qualifications
9+ years of experience in product design, UX or related product experience disciplines, including 3+ years managing product designers
Proven experience managing designers across complex B2B SaaS, platform, mobile or multi-product environments
Exceptional aesthetic judgment, visual craft and interaction-design taste, with the ability to raise the quality of work across a team
Experience leading critique, coaching designers and helping teams make strong design decisions
Experience leading or line managing design system work, including component libraries, shared patterns, contribution models, documentation, governance or adoption across product teams
Experience managing distributed teams and working across time zones; experience working closely with India-based teams is a strong plus
Demonstrated ability to hire strong designers, develop existing talent and performance manage team members who need additional support
Strong product judgment and comfort balancing customer needs, business outcomes, technical constraints and speed of execution
Familiarity with AI-assisted production tools such as Cursor, Claude Code or exploratory "vibe coding" workflows, and enthusiasm for using them thoughtfully to improve design velocity and collaboration
Comfort operating in fast-paced, ambiguous environments with high ownership expectations
What success looks like
Core platform and mobile experiences become more cohesive, intuitive and polished across the customer journey
HighLevel's bespoke design system becomes a major force for better UX/UI, with clearer strategy, stronger execution, broader adoption and visible improvements to customer-facing quality
The team's design output shows a step change in aesthetic quality, visual craft, interaction models, information architecture and end-to-end product thinking
Designers receive clearer feedback, stronger coaching and better development support across both US and India teams
The team embraces AI-assisted workflows to explore faster, communicate ideas more clearly and deliver better outcomes without compromising quality
Product, Engineering and other partners experience Design as a clear, reliable and high-quality partner in shaping and shipping product work

Lead design for foundational product experiences used by millions of businesses
Manage and grow a talented team across US and India
Help level up design system strategy and execution across a broad product platform
Raise the bar for aesthetic quality, craft, interaction quality and product design excellence
Work with modern AI-assisted production tools and workflows in a culture that values velocity, ownership and practical experimentation

jobs.title: Sr. Product Analyst – Lead Generation
jobs.description:
About HighLevel
About us
HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes.
To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently.
Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.

Our people
With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our impact
Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.

About the Team
The Lead Generation Team owns some of the most important products businesses use to build their digital presence and generate leads on HighLevel.
Our product portfolio includes Funnels, Websites, AI Studio, Forms, Surveys, Quizzes, Domains, Media, QR Codes, Listings, SEO, Analytics, Tracking, and other lead-generation experiences.
Millions of funnels, websites, forms, and other digital experiences are created using HighLevel. Our goal is to help agencies and businesses not only create these experiences but continuously improve their ability to attract visitors, capture leads, and drive conversions.
Data plays a critical role in how we make product decisions. We are looking for a Senior Product Analyst who can independently lead analytical work, deepen our understanding of customer behavior, identify growth opportunities, and help Product Managers make faster, better-informed decisions.
About the Role
HighLevel is looking for a highly analytical and product-minded Senior Product Analyst to join our Lead Generation Product team.
You will work closely with Product Managers, Engineering, Design, Data, and GTM teams to understand how customers discover, adopt, and use our products—and where the most meaningful opportunities exist to improve their experience.
You will own analytical projects end to end: framing the right questions, defining the approach, validating the data, conducting the analysis, and translating findings into clear recommendations. Your work will span the complete customer journey, from activation and feature adoption to engagement, conversion, retention, and monetization.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role with a strong emphasis on independent ownership, product judgment, and cross-functional influence. Beyond delivering reports, you will proactively surface opportunities, challenge assumptions, and help Product Managers determine what we should build, why we should build it, and whether what we shipped actually worked.
Responsibilities
Own end-to-end product analyses across Funnels, Websites, Forms, Surveys, Domains, SEO, Listings, and other LeadGen products, turning ambiguous questions into structured analyses and actionable recommendations.
Partner with Product Managers to define success metrics and measurement frameworks for product areas and initiatives, covering activation, adoption, engagement, retention, conversion, and monetization.
Build and maintain dashboards that give Product Managers and leadership clear visibility into product health, emerging trends, and business outcomes, while enabling teams to answer recurring questions independently.
Lead funnel and journey analyses to identify friction and drop-offs across onboarding, creation, publishing, lead capture, and other critical workflows.
Conduct cohort, segmentation, and retention analyses to understand differences across customer segments, usage patterns, and lifecycle stages—and identify where targeted improvements could have the greatest impact.
Partner with Product Managers to size opportunities, validate hypotheses, evaluate trade-offs, and prioritize initiatives based on potential customer and business impact.
Define measurement plans before feature launches, establish baselines, and evaluate adoption and outcomes after release. Communicate what the evidence supports, where uncertainty remains, and what to do next.
Partner with Product, Engineering, and Data teams to define events, properties, tracking requirements, and instrumentation, ensuring critical customer journeys can be measured reliably.
Proactively identify data quality issues and tracking gaps, investigate their impact, and work with relevant teams to improve the consistency and reliability of product analytics.
Designand analyze A/B tests and product experiments, including hypotheses, success metrics, guardrail metrics, and interpretation of results, to support statistically sound decisions.
Contribute to requirements definition and feature validation across multiple initiatives, including success criteria and pre-launch validation.
Lead customer research, including interviews and surveys, and combine it with quantitative data and support-ticket signalsLead deep-dive and root-cause analyses when important metrics change unexpectedly, distinguishing meaningful shifts from data issues, seasonality, or changes in customer mix.
Proactively recommend opportunities to improve lead generation, conversion rates, product adoption, engagement, and retention, and partner with teams to assess the results of resulting changes.
Present complex findings as clear, decision-oriented narratives, explaining recommendations, trade-offs, assumptions, and limitations to Product Managers, Engineering, Design, and leadership.
Contribute to shared analytical practices, metric definitions, and documentation, bringing customer and LeadGen domain context to the numbers rather than reporting metrics in isolation.
Mentor junior analysts and facilitate discovery discussions with Product, Design and Engineering
Requirements
4-7 years of experience in Product Analytics, Business Analytics, Data Analytics, or a related analytical role, with demonstrated experience informing product decisions.
Strong proficiency in SQL, including complex joins, window functions, and working independently with large datasets.
Demonstrated ability to own analytical projects end to end, from clarifying an ambiguous problem to delivering recommendations and following through on outcomes.
Experience leading customer research (interviews, surveys) and competitive analysis.
Experience with product analytics or BI tools such as Amplitude, Mixpanel, Pendo, Tableau, Looker, Power BI, or similar platforms.
Strong understanding of product metrics such as activation, adoption, engagement, retention, conversion, churn, and monetization, including how to select appropriate metrics for different product goals.
Hands-on experience with funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation, retention analysis, and user journey analysis.
Experience designing or analyzing A/B tests or product experiments, with a practical understanding of hypothesis testing, statistical significance, and common analytical biases.
Working knowledge of event-based analytics, instrumentation, and tracking plans, with experience identifying data quality issues and validating analytical inputs.
Strong proficiency with Excel or Google Sheets, along with the ability to build clear dashboards and communicate findings through effective data visualization.
Experience partnering closely with Product Managers, Engineering, Design, and other cross-functional teams to influence prioritization and product improvements.
Ability to communicate complex findings in simple business terms, make clear recommendations, and explain assumptions and limitations.
Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to prioritize analytical work based on its potential impact.
Nice to Have
Experience with Python for data analysis, including libraries such as Pandas and NumPy.
Familiarity with Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, pixels, attribution, or web analytics.
Understanding of websites, funnels, conversion rate optimization, digital marketing, or lead-generation products.
Experience working in B2B SaaS, MarTech, CRM, website builders, or high-growth technology companies.
Familiarity with APIs and an ability to understand how data flows between systems.
Experience improving analytics workflows, documenting reusable approaches, or helping teammates strengthen their analytical skills.
Preferred Soft Skills
Curiosity to go beyond what happened and understand why it happened and what we should do next.
Strong product and customer judgment, with the ability to connect analytical findings to real customer problems.
Comfort independently navigating ambiguity and balancing rigor with the need to make timely decisions.
Confidence to challenge assumptions constructively and influence decisions without formal authority.
Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to tailor the level of detail to the audience.
Strong ownership and collaboration skills in a fast-moving, remote environment.
What Success Looks Like
A successful Senior Product Analyst in the Lead Generation team will help us move from “we think this is happening” to “we understand what is happening, why it matters, and what we should do next.”
Product teams will have clearer success metrics, more reliable measurement, and a stronger understanding of customer behavior. Important opportunities and risks will be surfaced proactively, and launches and experiments will produce actionable learning—not just reports.
Your work will directly influence product strategy, roadmap prioritization, experimentation, and investment decisions across HighLevel’s Lead Generation portfolio.

Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We're proud to be a part of that.
ABOUT THE TEAM
The B2C/Creators Product team at HighLevel is focused on building and scaling a world-class learning experience for our customers and their audiences. The platform currently serves over 1.1 million monthly active users, making it one of HighLevel's most widely adopted products. This role offers a unique opportunity to operate at scale while solving B2C-style learner experience problems within a B2B2C product ecosystem.
Events is one of the newest products in HighLevel's Memberships suite, currently in beta and being built from the ground up. It gives our customers a native way to create, publish and sell events — in-person, online and hybrid — with ticketing, RSVPs, paid and free registration, and attendee management, sitting directly alongside the contacts, communities, courses, credentials and automations they already run their business on. Organizers build and run their events from the Memberships admin; attendees live the whole thing inside Client Portal, next to the courses, communities and credentials they already sign in for.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Own and Shape the B2C & Events Roadmap Partner with product leadership to help shape and execute the roadmap for HighLevel's B2C platform, serving 1.1M+ monthly active learners, with a focus on engagement, completion, and retention in a B2B2C environment.
Close the Table-Stakes Gap, Then Go Past It – Know the category cold. Get the expected capabilities right — ticket tiers, promo codes, capacity and waitlists, recurring and series events, refunds, embeddable widgets, calendar sync, wallet passes — and then decide deliberately where we go further than the incumbents rather than matching them feature for feature.
Take Events from Beta to GA – Own the beta exit criteria: the quality bar, the reliability bar, the feature completeness, and the adoption and revenue signals that tell us this product is ready to be sold broadly. Drive the program that closes those gaps.
Build Ticketing, Checkout and Payments – Lead paid, free and RSVP event types, multi-tier and multi-currency ticketing, checkout conversion, discounts, taxes, refunds and payouts — with the precision and trust a revenue-bearing flow demands, and with fee and payout terms that are a reason to choose us rather than a reason to resent us.
Give Organizers Ownership of Their Audience – Build the capability that most defines us against the category: every registration flows into the organizer's own CRM, segmentable, automatable and theirs to keep. Turn attendee data ownership from a talking point into the product's most obvious advantage.
Own Event-Day Operations – Events are judged on the day they happen. Own check-in and QR scanning, offline resilience at the door, guest lists and comp tickets, on-site sales, capacity enforcement and the operational tooling organizers depend on when things go wrong in real time.
Own the Attendee Experience in Client Portal – Client Portal is where the attendee side of Events lives, and you own it: how members find what is on, register and check out, hold their tickets, receive reminders and joining links, attend in person or online, and look back at what they have been to. Deliver that journey across both web and mobile, make events feel native to the portal rather than bolted onto it, and hold a phone-first bar throughout.
Drive Distribution and Discovery – Shape how events get found and filled: SEO-ready event pages, social and calendar syndication, embeddable listings, the Gokollab Marketplace, and the promotion tooling that turns an organizer's existing audience into attendance.
Open the Platform – Treat APIs, webhooks and integrations as a first-class surface rather than a premium upsell, so agencies and developers can build events into the workflows and client solutions they already sell.
Champion UI/UX Excellence – Partner closely with design and engineering to deliver interfaces that are intuitive, accessible, mobile-friendly and fast — for both the organizer building an event and the attendee registering for one.
Talk to Organizers Constantly – Run discovery with beta organizers, sit in on their setup, watch where they stall, and turn qualitative signal into a prioritized backlog. At this stage, direct customer contact is a primary input, not a supplement.
Experiment and Optimize – Design and analyze experiments across the funnel — event page conversion, registration completion, checkout drop-off, organizer onboarding — and iterate rapidly on evidence rather than opinion.
Support Scale, Reliability and Trust – Drive the platform work a live-event product demands: registration integrity, capacity and waitlist correctness, payment reliability, fraud and listing trust, and graceful behavior under the traffic spikes that come with a popular event going on sale.
Collaborate Cross-Functionally – Work across engineering, design, data, support, marketing and customer-facing teams to launch features, drive adoption, and close the loop on organizer feedback.
Define and Own the Metrics – Establish the success metrics for a product that does not yet have them — organizer activation, time to first published event, repeat-event rate, registration and checkout conversion, attendance rate, gross ticket volume and revenue per organizer — set the OKRs against them, and use them to steer the roadmap.
Deliver Outcomes, Not Just Features – Be accountable for measurable growth in events published, organizers activated, registrations processed and ticket revenue running through the platform.
WHO YOU ARE
B2C Experience – You have built and shipped impactful features for B2C platforms or content products, creating engaging end user experiences that drive activation, completion, and retention at meaningful scale.
An End-to-End Owner – You are comfortable owning the entire life of an event across two connected surfaces: the creator experience in the Memberships admin, where an organizer builds, prices, publishes, promotes and runs their event, and the attendee experience in Client Portal, where a member discovers it, registers, attends and looks back on it. You think in terms of the whole journey and the handoffs between those surfaces, not in terms of screens.
UX-Attentive for Learning – You bring a strong UI/UX sensibility focused on learner journeys, content discovery, progress tracking, and habit formation, with a track record of delivering intuitive and high-quality learning experiences.
Experimentation-Minded – You are comfortable running A/B tests and structured experiments to improve learner engagement and completion rates through rapid, evidence-based iteration.
Learner-Centric – You consistently balance business objectives with learner success, keeping learner needs, motivation, and outcomes at the center of product decisions.
Customer-Obsessed – You seek out organizers directly, run your own discovery, and can translate what you hear into product decisions without waiting for a research team to formalize it.
Strategic and Execution-Focused – You can contribute meaningfully to product vision while staying deeply involved in day-to-day execution to ensure ideas translate into real, measurable impact.
Data-Informed – You rely on behavioral data, funnel metrics, and cohort analysis to prioritize initiatives, validate assumptions, and guide product decisions.
WHAT YOU'LL BRING
7+ years of Product Management experience, with meaningful exposure to events, ticketing, marketplace, commerce or B2B2C SaaS products.
Proven track record of taking a product from early stage to scaled adoption, with clear ownership of the decisions that made it work.
Hands-on experience with monetization mechanics — checkout, pricing and packaging, payments, refunds, payouts and fee structure — and the operational realities that come with them.
Working knowledge of the events and ticketing category, including how platforms such as Eventbrite, Luma, Meetup and Cvent are positioned, priced and differentiated.
Solid understanding of UI/UX principles, with the ability to partner closely with design to deliver intuitive, accessible and high-quality journeys for two distinct user types: organizers and attendees.
Familiarity with SaaS and B2C platform growth levers, including user activation, engagement loops, retention, lifecycle optimization, and audience monetization.
Comfort operating with ambiguity, incomplete data and shifting priorities in a fast-moving, remote-first environment.
Bonus: You have worked on an events, ticketing or community platform and can clearly articulate your personal impact on organizer growth, conversion and revenue.
WHY SHOULD YOU JOIN US?
At HighLevel, we foster an exciting and dynamic work environment driven by a passionate team. We believe in a collective responsibility where no task is considered someone else's job. Our unwavering focus is on providing value to our users, and we achieve this by delivering solutions swiftly through lean principles, allowing us to bring products to market in a matter of weeks rather than quarters.

We prioritise the well-being of our team, recognizing that by taking care of them, they can better serve our users. We embrace the concept of continuous and iterative improvement, understanding that progress is an ongoing journey. We are also a well funded & profitable company.
Join us at HighLevel, and you will have the opportunity to learn the intricacies of scaling a B2B SaaS startup and develop impactful products that cater to the needs of our customers.

Product engineers build the features. This role owns what the features stand on, the queues, the storage layers, the caching, the infrastructure, and makes sure it holds when the growth curve does what our growth curve does.

We're looking for the engineer who understands the whole vertical: how a query plan behaves at 1.5 TB of indexes, why a pod eviction turned into a message backlog, what a Redis failover actually does to the request path. Databases, infra, cloud, you see through all of it.

Team & System Overview:
The Conversations organization powers multi-channel communication across SMS, Email, WhatsApp, and DMs — handling over 2B messages each month. The Threads & Composer team owns the inbox and composer surfaces, and the backend services that deliver and store those interactions.You’ll work across Node.js microservices, GCP-based infra (GKE, Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks), and MongoDB/Firestore storage layers, ensuring every message and UI state stays consistent, fast, and recoverable.

Design and build the platform components Workflows and Conversations run on, queueing pipelines, storage access layers, caching strategies, rate limiters, schedulers

Own your components end to end: architecture, design docs, code, tests, rollout, dashboards, and production health

Go deep on data stores at scale, schema and index design, sharding strategies, replication behavior, and migrations on live systems with billions of records

Work close to the infrastructure: GKE autoscaling, resource tuning, Pub/Sub and Cloud Tasks topologies, and the capacity planning that keeps headroom ahead of growth

Spot gaps in your systems before production does, missing idempotency, unbounded queues, cache stampedes, hot shards, and drive the fixes

Debug the incidents that cross layers, where the answer isn't in one service's logs but in how the pieces interact

Write design docs and RCAs that make the platform's behavior legible to 80+ engineers building on it

Runtime: Node.js (TypeScript), Go, on GKE

Messaging & async: GCP Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks, Redis

Storage: MongoDB, Firestore, ClickHouse, ElasticSearch

Observability: metrics, tracing, and alerting you'll help make sharper

4+ years of backend engineering experience, with deep hands-on work in Node.js and/or Go

Strong systems understanding across the stack, application, database, and infrastructure, proven on high-throughput production systems

Deep experience with queueing and async processing, Pub/Sub, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Cloud Tasks, or similar, delivery semantics, ordering, backpressure, idempotency

Database depth beyond CRUD, indexing strategies, sharding, replication, query performance, and safe migrations on SQL or NoSQL stores at scale

Hands-on with Redis or other in-memory stores, caching patterns, data structures, and their failure modes

Production experience with cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, autoscaling, resource limits, and how they behave under pressure (GCP preferred)

You write clear design docs and rigorous test cases as a habit, not on request

Champion of AI-assisted engineering, you make agents produce accurate, production-quality code, fast

We are responsible for:
Email Platform: The Vue.js apps used to design, compose and send emails, plus the Node.js/NestJS services behind them.
Sending Infrastructure & Deliverability: IP pools, dedicated IPs, dedicated domains and shared domain pools. These let new users send from day one, while we stay accountable for getting their email into the inbox.
API-First Platform: Every capability is exposed through APIs, so email can be built into any product or workflow that needs it.
Scale & Reliability: Keeping throughput high at peak load, with high uptime and send success rates.
Email Statistics & Analytics: Integrating email stats with internal teams and making every release measurable on our dashboards.
AI in Email: Bringing LLM-powered capabilities into email creation, while weighing token cost, latency and quality
Impact & Scale
Email is one of the most critical channels on HighLevel. When it works, businesses grow; when it breaks, their customers stop hearing from them. That's the weight this role carries.
Businesses: Every one of the 1M+ businesses on HighLevel relies on email to reach their customers.
Sub-accounts: Your work runs across 1.6M+ sub-accounts, from solo operators to agencies managing hundreds of clients.
End users: What you ship reaches end users through 1.2B+ emails every month.
Volume: 40M+ emails a day flow through the systems you'll own, so a 1% gain in reliability or deliverability affects hundreds of thousands of emails daily.
Blast radius: One change can affect every business on the platform at once, which is why we care so much about reliability, data integrity and security.
How we work
Iterate fast: Go from idea to prototype to production in days, not quarters. Ship small, measure, learn and improve.
Use AI well: Use AI across the whole cycle (design, coding, testing, reviews and debugging) to move faster without lowering the quality bar, and pick the right model for each job based on quality, latency and cost.
About the Role:
The traditional model of siloed product managers, designers and engineers is too slow for AI-native development. At HighLevel, every engineer owns a product outcome end to end, from idea to prototype to production to scale. You will operate as a Team of One. Translate business goals into working, deployable systems.

Propose architecture, data models, workflows and implementation plans for your modules, then refine them with Tech Leads and Engineering Managers before you build.

Own modules end to end: design, release, post-launch stability and ongoing improvements.

Design clean, versioned, well-documented APIs as a core part of every feature, so the platform can be integrated wherever it's needed.

Turn ambiguous ideas into working demos quickly, using AI to build and iterate fast.

Validate through experiments and real user feedback, then iterate to production quality.

Drive feature attribution and metrics visibility so every release is measurable.

Scale, Performance & Reliability

Build and maintain the Email ecosystem, designing for scalability, reliability and data integrity at 40M+ emails/day.

Evolve our sending infrastructure, including IP pool management, dedicated IPs and domains, and shared domain pools, to protect sender reputation and maximize inbox placement.

Build robust error handling: idempotent processing, retries with backoff and graceful degradation.

Optimize frontend rendering, component architecture, lazy loading and state management. Tune backend queries, caching (Redis/CDN) and latency at scale.

Design data models and analytics on ClickHouse, MongoDB and Firestore.

Reason through token consumption, inference cost and infrastructure tradeoffs when integrating AI and LLMs.

Engineering Quality & Security

Practice test-driven development and hold a high bar for automated test coverage.

Build securely by default: authentication, secrets management and safe handling of customer data and PII.

Operational Excellence

Instrument systems with monitoring and telemetry.

Build evaluation loops for continuous quality improvement.

Automate workflows that increase engineering velocity.

Keep documentation clear and repeatable.

4+ years building and running production systems, including owning them when they broke: the on-call, the incident and the fix.

Experience with Go (Golang).

Deep proficiency with protobuf + ConnectRPC/gRPC and API lifecycle management (versioning, compatibility, contract testing, Buf)

About the Team
Even a simple configuration error can lead to significant unintended usage. At HighLevel, we aim to build robust systems that protect our customers and the platform from accidental surges and intentional abuse alike. This team creates the intelligent safeguards that ensure our automation remains safe and reliable for everyone.
We are looking for a Staff Engineer to architect the future of Trust, Controls & Safety. You will lead the technical direction of a real-time platform that secures critical workflows across HighLevel—including Signups, SaaS checkouts, User management, and global communication usage. This system processes 160M+ events and $4M+ in transactions daily, serving as the essential foundation for platform integrity.
The challenge is to build a highly available, low-latency control plane that balances strict enforcement with a seamless user experience. By integrating synchronous metering with asynchronous signal correlation, you will help us stay ahead of evolving fraud vectors while ensuring that legitimate business activities, from new user signups to complex SaaS billing cycles, proceed without friction.
As a Staff Engineer, you'll set the technical direction, own the hardest problems on the platform, mentor engineers across squads, and partner closely with EMs, PMs, Finance, Risk, Support and the channel teams. Getting this right means customers stop getting bills they didn't intend, and abuse stops being a cost the honest majority carries.

Database architecture: Redesign and optimize data models, queries, and indexing strategies across MongoDB, Firestore, and ElasticSearch

Search at scale: Own ElasticSearch reliability — ingestion, indexing, shard strategy, and query performance for billions of documents

Reliability & performance: Eliminate bottlenecks, improve replication health, and enforce predictable query and index latency

System design: Define data flow and integration boundaries between storage, cache, and APIs with clear contracts and fault isolation

Observability: Build visibility into every data path — metrics, traces, slow query logs, replication lag, and cluster health dashboards

Testing & quality: Make testing non-negotiable — enforce unit, integration, and load testing standards across all backend modules

Engineering culture: Drive RFCs, ADRs, and design reviews that push clarity and precision. Codify patterns that make good engineering repeatable

Hands-on leadership: Write code, design systems, and debug production issues. Lead by technical example, not by delegation

Mentorship & influence: Level up engineers around you — reviews that teach, feedback that sticks, and systems that outlive individuals
Requirements
Heavyweight Engineering Pedigree: 8+ years of experience building high-scale, mission-critical backend systems where p99 regressions are unacceptable.

Distributed Systems Mastery: Deep expertise in concurrency, event-driven architectures, and consistency primitives (CAS, atomic dry-runs, idempotency).

Financial Rigor: Experience with systems where code correctness has direct financial impact—metering, ledgers, or payment gateways.

Operational Instinct: A track record of technical leadership through influence, driving architecture for multi-team platforms from design to production.

Experience with systems where correctness has financial consequences — metering, ledgers, billing, reservations, or comparable transactional domains

Strong experience with relational and NoSQL data models (especially with complex transactional data), plus working knowledge of streaming and analytical stores for time-windowed aggregation

Experience designing policy- or rules-driven systems that change through configuration rather than deploys — versioning, safe rollout, and rollback of behavioural change

Sound judgement on the enforcement trade-off: how to set thresholds and actions that stop real harm without punishing legitimate customers, and how to measure whether you got it right

Familiarity with monitoring, SLOs, and root-cause analysis in production environments

Familiarity with hallucination mitigation strategies (e.g., code constraints, test scaffolding, embeddings, context injection)

Track record of technical leadership without formal authority — driving cross-team architecture to a decision, writing designs others build from, and lifting the engineering standard around you

Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills, including with Finance, Risk and Support stakeholders

A pragmatic, hands-on engineer who balances long-term vision with iterative execution

Familiarity with ClickHouse or other OLAP systems for analytics

Background in event-driven systems, data pipelines, or message brokers

Contributions to open-source or public technical writing on database performance or systems design

Abuse & Fraud Expertise: Experience building rules engines, velocity checks, or adversarial defense systems at massive scale.

Modern Data Stack: Hands-on with high-throughput tools like Go, Redis (Lua), ClickHouse, and Flink for real-time aggregation.

Exposure to stream processing at scale (Flink, Kafka Streams, Beam) and columnar analytical stores (ClickHouse, BigQuery) for real-time aggregation

About the Role:
We're hiring a Staff Data Scientist, Core Revenue Retention to own one outcome — keeping and growing revenue from existing customers — across every team that shapes it. Revenue retention isn't the property of a single product: it spans CPaaS (phone, SMS, email, WhatsApp) as our largest MRR surface, add-on monetization including emerging AI features, the Customer Success motions that protect accounts, and Finance's forecasts.

This is a broad, cross-functional role. You'll work closely with Communications/CPaaS, Customer Success, the AI teams pursuing add-on revenue, Finance, and other revenue-driving product teams; you report centrally to Product Analytics & Data Science for craft and standards and carry the revenue-retention outcome across organizational boundaries. You'll build the retention/value model, separate real churn signal from data-maturity and mix artifacts, and turn diagnosis into a prioritized, evidence-based retention and add-on-monetization agenda. You'll work amid a data foundation still being built, consuming governed sources rather than rebuilding them, and raising the bar as you go. This is a hands-on, direction-setting Staff role — you advise Customer Success, Finance, and CPaaS leaders and set retention-measurement standards that analysts on adjacent teams adopt, with a path to grow a pod as the mandate scales.
Responsibilities:
Own the causal read on core revenue retention and add-on monetization — gross and net revenue retention, MRR churn (voluntary vs involuntary), attach and usage of add-ons — across CPaaS, AI add-ons, and other revenue surfaces

Quantify add-on revenue opportunity across CPaaS and emerging AI features, and the drivers behind attach and consumption

Apply rigorous causal inference (matching, diff-in-diff, survival/hazard, synthetic control) where clean experiments aren't feasible — separating real signal from selection bias, seasonality, and mix

Partner with Finance/RevOps on single-source-of-truth definitions and forecasting inputs; drive the revenue-retention insights

Partner with the Product Strategy & Growth org on the TTP/churn charter, and with the Experimentation lead to test retention interventions rigorously

Act as a trusted analytical advisor to Customer Success, Finance, and Communications/CPaaS leaders, and set the analytical standards that DS and analysts on adjacent teams adopt — raising the bar without direct authority

Set the technical direction for how revenue retention is measured company-wide — own the canonical GRR/NRR, churn, and add-on metrics on governed, certified data that other teams build on; shape the taxonomy retention analytics depends on with Analytics Engineering

Build the retention and causal-inference framework — the standards and reusable methods (survival/hazard, diff-in-diff, synthetic control) that Analytics Engineering and adjacent DS teams reuse beyond this mandate

Use AI tooling (Claude and similar) to move faster on exploration, documentation, and analysis
Requirements:
9+ years in revenue/retention analytics, data science, or applied statistics, with deep experience on churn, retention, and monetization

Practical causal inference with sound judgment about when a result is causal vs. an artifact of how the data was generated

Comfort untangling messy financial/billing/usage data and defining metrics that survive scrutiny from Finance and product alike

Strong SQL and working proficiency in Python; comfort in a Snowflake + dbt environment

Track record where a retention or monetization diagnosis changed a product, pricing, CS, or lifecycle decision

Comfort amid imperfect, in-progress data — you consume governed sources and raise the bar rather than rebuilding pipelines

Cross-functional influence — you align product, Customer Success, Finance, and leadership on shared numbers without direct authority
Nice to Have:
CPaaS (telephony/messaging) or usage-based/consumption revenue experience

B2B SaaS or CRM background; experience with MRR/subscription billing, dunning, and involuntary-churn recovery

Familiarity with Statsig or a comparable experimentation platform

Exposure to AI-assisted analytics workflows; experience mentoring analysts
Success in this role looks like:
CPaaS, AI add-ons, and Customer Success act on your model, and drives strong positive business results.

Finance/RevOps and Product Analytics report the consistent metrics with clear insight and recommendations.

Leaders across the revenue domain make roadmap and spend calls off your analysis, not gut feel

The revenue-retention mandate has reusable patterns and the foundation to scale beyond one IC

A successful Staff Engineer:

Designs systems that remain reliable as traffic and data volume grow significantly

Solves architectural problems that affect multiple services and engineering teams

Identifies scalability and reliability risks before they become production incidents

Improves latency, throughput, availability, and infrastructure efficiency

Our people

We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our impact
Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.
Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts

What are we hiring for?
Our teams are strong at building and scaling products. Every service has an owner, every feature has engineers behind it, and every database has deep expertise. What we need now is someone who can look across all of them — someone who understands how the entire distributed system works together and can identify risks that may not be visible within an individual service.
A retry policy in one service, combined with a queue configuration several hops downstream, can become a cascading failure under peak load. Your role is to identify those risks before they reach production.
You’ll start with Workflows, HighLevel’s automation engine and one of the largest systems in the company. It handles 3.1 billion enrollments and 21.5 billion action executions every month, with traffic peaking at 28,000+ requests per second. The platform runs across thousands of pods on GCP and uses Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks, Redis, and multiple database engines.
From there, your scope will expand into Conversations, which processes 2.6 billion messages every month, as well as our new Ticketing platform. With Ticketing, you’ll have the opportunity to influence the architecture early — building resilience and scalability into the system from the start rather than addressing them later.
This is not a traditional architect role where you design systems and hand them over for implementation. It is also not a feature-focused engineering role with a defined product backlog.
This role sits across systems and teams, with a clear mandate: understand how the platform behaves as a whole, identify systemic risks, and make sure our architecture can continue to scale reliably.
Responsibilities:
Own the architecture health of a billion-scale distributed system, its failure modes, capacity limits, consistency guarantees, and the interactions between 50+ deployments that no single team can see

Approve critical-path designs. Changes that touch the system's core go through you, not as bureaucracy, but as the person accountable for the whole staying sound. When there's a disagreement, you make your case on merit

Hunt gaps proactively, single points of failure, unbounded queues, missing idempotency, thundering herds, quiet data-loss windows, and drive the fixes before they become incidents

Build the parts nobody else can. No sprint tickets. You prototype the risky architectural bets yourself, ship the remediation after serious incidents, and pair into the gnarliest cross-team bugs, roughly a quarter to a third of your time in code, all of it on the hardest problems

Make resilience a property of the system, not a heroic act, degradation strategies, backpressure, isolation boundaries, capacity models that survive 10%+ month-over-month growth

Raise the teams around you. Design reviews that teach, post-mortems that change architecture (not just add alerts), and patterns that 80+ engineers build on

Set the standard for how AI-assisted engineering works safely on systems this critical, where a bad merge doesn't cost a demo, it costs real businesses their revenue

The terrain:

Runtime: Node.js (TypeScript), Go, thousands of pods on GKE

Messaging & async: GCP Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks, Redis

Storage: MongoDB, Firestore, ClickHouse, ElasticSearch

Scale: 21.5B automation actions/month, 2.6B messages/month, 28.5K req/s peaks, ~226B async events across the org
Requirements:
10+ years of engineering experience with deep, hands-on ownership of large-scale distributed systems, comparable scale strongly preferred: hundreds of services or thousands of instances, billions of daily events

You've carried sole accountability for a production system through real failures, not adjacent to it, not advising on it. Owned it

Deep command of queueing and async architectures, delivery semantics, ordering, backpressure, idempotency, exactly-once myths and at-least-once realities

Strong with multiple storage engines (SQL and NoSQL), you reason about consistency models, indexing at scale, and when each engine is the wrong choice

Expert-level depth in Redis or comparable in-memory systems, including their failure modes under memory pressure and network partition

Production experience on Kubernetes at scale, resource limits, autoscaling behavior, what actually happens when a node pool dies

Exceptional design communication, docs, diagrams, and RCAs that drive decisions across multiple teams

Fluent in Node.js and/or Go, enough to prototype your own proposals and ship fixes on the critical path
What Success Looks Like
The critical paths of Workflows have named owners, capacity models, and tested failure modes, because you made it so

Incident count trends down while traffic grows double-digit percent month over month

Your design reviews are the ones engineers want their proposals to survive

Your scope has expanded on results, more systems, more surface, more trust
What you're built for
You've been injured in production. A lot. You've owned distributed systems at serious scale, through the outages, the migrations, the 3 AM discoveries, and every scar changed how you design

You've operated at staff scope, whatever your title said, the engineer everyone routed the hardest systems questions to

You think in failure modes by default: when you see a design, you instinctively ask what happens at the tail, under partition, at 10x load

You write design docs and RCAs that people reference years later, clear trade-offs, honest risks, real recommendations

You can disagree with a team and still make them better, influence through rigor and respect, not title

You'd rather prevent ten incidents quietly than be the hero of one loudly
Bonus Points
You've made AI agents genuinely productive on complex systems, and know how to keep AI-generated code from becoming AI-generated incidents

GCP-native experience: Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks, GKE, Firestore

You've done this job before under another name, "the systems person," principal engineer, architect-who-still-codes

Experience taking a 0→1 system to production alongside hardening mature ones

About the Role:

Our stack is primarily Vue 3; strong engineers from React, Angular, or Svelte backgrounds are welcome, and existing Vue experience is a plus.
Responsibilities:
Failure Isolation: Design so a broken or slow remote degrades one surface, not the whole application — with fallbacks, timeouts, and the observability to identify which remote caused an incident.

Release Strategy: Own the deployment and versioning story for independent releases, including contract testing across host/remote boundaries, staged rollout, and fast rollback of a single remote.

Load Performance: Attack bundle size and dependency-graph bloat through code splitting, shared-chunk strategy across federated remotes, preloading/prefetching, and caching/CDN strategy.

Runtime Performance: Attack main-thread cost through long-task analysis, reactivity and re-render cost, list virtualization, and memory leak diagnosis in long-lived sessions. You're the person engineers escalate production-only regressions and render thrash to.

Performance Measurement: Define the metrics that matter (Core Web Vitals, INP, route transition time), instrument them in real-user monitoring, and enforce budgets in CI so regressions are caught before they ship.

Quality Bar: Set and enforce accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA), internationalization, and cross-browser support through automated checks, not documentation alone.

Technical Leadership: Write proposals that build genuine consensus, review designs and code where decisions are expensive to reverse, and mentor senior and mid-level engineers across the org.

9+ years of front-end development experience.

Expert-level JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS, with a first-principles understanding of the browser — rendering/layout, the event loop, network/caching, and memory.

Deep production experience with a modern component framework. Primarily Vue 3 (Composition API); strong React, Angular, or Svelte experience is welcome if you're willing to go deep on Vue.

Demonstrated architectural ownership — you've defined a front-end architecture and moved a real codebase from one state to another without freezing feature work.

Hands-on production experience with micro-frontends or module federation, including the failure modes. Equivalent experience decomposing a large monolith by other means also considered.

Proven track record optimizing large-scale, complex web applications. Be ready to walk through a specific example with numbers.

Experience with modern build tooling at scale (Vite, Webpack, Rspack, Turborepo, or Nx), with enough depth to debug the build when it breaks.

Working knowledge of accessibility as an engineering discipline — semantics, focus/keyboard behavior, ARIA where genuinely needed, screen reader testing.

Strong written communication. On a remote-first, async team, most of your influence travels as design docs, RFCs, and PR descriptions.

A track record of mentoring engineers and driving change across teams you don't manage.

Nice to have: familiarity with Node.js, server-side rendering, and open-source contributions.
What You'll Lead:
The target architecture for our front-end, and the migrations that get us there — sequenced into reversible steps, driven with codemods and adoption metrics, agreed across teams rather than imposed on them.

The application shell and its contracts: bootstrapping, routing, auth-aware navigation, error and loading boundaries, and cross-application state.

Our module federation topology: host and remote boundaries, shared dependency and singleton management, and version skew between independently deployed remotes.

The shared component library and design system implementation, with APIs that are hard to misuse and safe to version.

Our People
